yes_case.case: The closest past historical episodes for establishing high-tech domestic missile manufacturing under acute wartime duress are the rapid localization of Ukrainian 'Neptune' anti-ship cruise missile production following the 2022 invasion, and the underground dispersal of Bayraktar drone manufacturing facilities. This case differs significantly from the Neptune precedent because the SCALP/Storm Shadow is a sophisticated Western-supplied cruise missile involving highly sensitive British and French intellectual property, restricted turbojet components, and specialized guidance systems, whereas the Neptune was an indigenous post-Soviet design. However, it differs favorably from past Western technology transfers due to the unprecedented desperation driven by intense Russian aerial attacks battering Kyiv and multiple regions, which forces an aggressive acceleration of joint-venture decentralization. Unlike the historical precedent of lengthy, bureaucratic defense procurement cycles, the existential pressure of continuous bombardment collapses the timeline for technology transfer, making the establishment of a domestic assembly or component-manufacture line for Storm Shadow variants vastly more attainable than standard peacetime co-production models suggest.
key_evidence: Intense Russian aerial attacks battering Kyiv and multiple regions creating acute existential pressure for deep localization.
Historical precedent of Ukraine's rapid adaptation and domestic scaling of the Neptune cruise missile system.

no_case.case: The strongest case for a NO resolution relies on examining past complex Western-to-Eastern European defense technology transfers—specifically the local integration of advanced Western air defense components in Soviet-era platforms (such as the FrankenSAM initiatives converting Buk systems to use RIM-7 Sea Sparrow or AIM-9M missiles) and the localized maintenance hubs attempted for Leopard tanks. This case differs from those past episodes because a SCALP/Storm Shadow is not a modular surface-to-air missile or a heavy armored chassis; it is an air-launched, low-observable cruise missile requiring highly sensitive guidance systems, specialized composite airframes, and precise turbojet integration that dwarfs the technological threshold of previous domestic adaptations. Unlike past episodes of rapid adaptation or field-jury-rigging, establishing a full sovereign production line for a deep-strike cruise missile under persistent, intense Russian aerial attacks (as documented in Kyiv and multiple regions) faces an insurmountable security and precision-manufacturing deficit that historical precedents of localized maintenance or minor component assembly simply did not encounter.
